validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real and independently confirmed by three separate origins. (1) NS Energy Business (nsenergybusiness.com/projects/leidy-south/, a GlobalData project-database profile) states Williams filed the expansion with FERC in August 2019, FERC approved it July 2020, and gives a full engineering description: replacement of ~10km of existing 24in Leidy Line A with 36in pipe in Clinton County PA, a 3.86km 36in 'Hilltop loop' in Clinton County, and a 5.63km 42in 'Benton loop' in Lycoming County, plus compressor uprates/additions at stations 605 (Wyoming Co), 607 (Luzerne Co, greenfield), 610 (Columbia Co) and 620 (Schuylkill Co); factbox: Capacity 582,400 Dth/d, Estimated Investment $531m, Start of Construction 2020, Expected Completion December 2021, Owner/Operator Williams (subsidiary Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company / Transco). (2) Pipeline & Gas Journal (pgjonline.com, 2020-07-20, trade press, independent of NS Energy) confirms FERC approval, 582,400 Dth/d of added capacity, '6.3 miles of existing pipe replacement, 5.9 miles of new pipeline loop segments,' completion targeted for the 2021-2022 winter heating season, and explicitly names Transco as the operating system. (3) The EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects.xlsx, 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' tab, row for 'Leidy South Project' / operator 'Transcontinental Gas Pipeline') is a fully independent US government source and lists: Status=Completed, Completed Date 2021-12-15, Year In Service 2021, State(s)=PA, Beg_State=PA, End_State=PA, Cost $531 million, Miles 12.2, Additional Capacity 580 MMcf/d, Diameter '36,42', Interstate -- an exact match on every spec GEM already carries for this row (Length 12.20mi, Diameter 36/42in, Capacity 580 MMcf/d, SegmentCost $531,000,000, StartYear1 2021, Status operating). This is not a GEM-only entity: no traces in the harvested pool cite GEM or gem.wiki. CLASSIFICATION: correctly recorded as a gas transmission-system expansion (FERC-jurisdictional interstate pipeline, Transco/Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company) -- loop segments + a pipe-diameter upgrade + compressor additions, not a gathering/processing line. Confirmed by all three sources plus EIA's own 'Interstate' / 'Expansion' project-type tags. DUPLICATE: checked against the 46-row roster -- no other row in this batch describes the same physical work. One genealogy note worth flagging for a future Discovery pass (not actioned here, out of scope for a validity sweep): the EIA workbook also carries a DIFFERENT, EARLIER 'Leidy South Project' (operator 'Dominion Transmission', completed 2017-09-27, PA-MD-VA, 155 MMcf/d, $210m) -- NS Energy explicitly describes THIS Williams/Transco expansion as 'an enhancement to the existing Leidy South pipeline developed by Dominion Transmission in October 2017.' GEM's P2551 row specs (12.2mi/580 MMcf/d/$531m) match only the 2021 Transco project, not the 2017 Dominion one -- no double-count risk for P2551 itself, but the 2017 Dominion 'Leidy South' project does not appear anywhere in this 46-row roster and may be a genuine gap GEM has never tracked (a name collision analogous to the Mountaineer XPress / Mountaineer Gas Company cluster flagged for this batch, just not one of the 46 rows in scope here).

validity.researcher_notes: GEM currently records StartState/Province=Pennsylvania (correct) and EndState/Province=Delaware (wrong). All three independent sources describe this project as confined entirely to Pennsylvania: NS Energy says the corridor 'covers three counties in the northcentral region and the other three in the northeast region' of PA's DEP jurisdiction (Clinton, Lycoming, Wyoming, Luzerne, Columbia, Schuylkill counties are the only ones named); Pipeline & Gas Journal frames the whole project as PA construction serving demand further down the Atlantic Seaboard, never itself extending into Delaware; and the EIA workbook's own State(s)/Beg_State/End_State fields for this exact row all read 'PA' -- no MD, DE, or other state code appears. The gem.wiki page's own Location line ('The pipeline would run through Pennsylvania, Maryland, and Delaware, USA') is very likely where the Delaware value originated, but that line appears to conflate the built project's physical footprint with its downstream MARKET reach -- the wiki's own Background text says 'The pipeline expanded deliverability to the Cove Point LNG Terminal on the Transco system,' and Cove Point LNG is in Calvert County, MARYLAND (not Delaware), reached via Transco's broader Zone 5/6 network rather than by any pipe segment built in this project. (Read gem.wiki for this lead only -- not cited as a reference.) Net: EndState/Province should read Pennsylvania, matching StartState/Province and all three independent, on-topic sources. No fills[] object is staged for the Location [ref] cluster because the current EndState/Province value is disputed, not merely unsourced -- adding a ref there would look like confirmation of the wrong state.
